title: Atmosphere / drone synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic stereo atmosphere or drone (v0.1, proposal, #526, D-034; input: docs/research/2026-11-08_parking-atmos-drones.md section 6, with the #525 review points fixed). Output shape (n, 2). Only schema_version, seed and bpm are required. The file is a tempo-bound loop of `bars` 4/4 bars at `bpm` that loops seamlessly by construction (loop_mode seamless, the default), or a one-shot with fades and an optional tail (loop_mode oneshot). Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. One shared parameter space for four kinds (`kind`: noise_bed, drone, resonant, granular); a kind sets which sources are rendered and the DEFAULTS of the per-kind fields, never which fields exist. A field a kind (or the loop_mode) does not use has no effect. PER-KIND DEFAULTS LIVE IN THIS FILE, as in fx-params: a field whose default depends on the kind has no top-level `default`; its default for each kind is the `default` annotation inside that kind's branch of `allOf` (the noise_bed branch also applies when `kind` is omitted, because noise_bed is the default kind). No field has a derived default (no `x-derived-default` annotation): the note's hp_hz = 0.8 * f0 proposal for the tonal kinds is replaced by a fixed per-kind value, because x-derived-default copies a field and cannot express a formula. The engine resolves top-level defaults first, then the kind branch, and the sidecar records the fully resolved object. Presets are named overrides on top of these defaults, not a second source of defaults. All ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS: no number was measured against a reference and nothing was listened to; only the 4-bar filter LFO (move_cycles 2 at 8 bars), the high- plus low-pass of a noise bed, the 400 Hz 'dark' reverb high cut (reverb_damp_hz floor 300) and the mono-below-120 Hz default rest on a source (note A2, A3, A6). Not part of v0.1: own library WAVs as a granular source, spectral freeze, key or note-name resolution from an arrangement plan, odd meters, tempo changes inside a file, writing clip warp/loop settings in Live (D-034 item 4), synth voices (D-034 item 3), a planner adapter.
$comment: Contract rules that JSON Schema cannot express or that are not field ranges. sr = sample_rate. (1) Length: the loop has N = round(240 * bars * sr / bpm) frames (double precision; round half to even, as Python round: 1 bar at 128 BPM and 44.1 kHz is 82687.5 -> 82688). N is the exact musical length only when 240 * bars * sr / bpm is an integer. Of the whole-number tempos 120-150 BPM: at 48000 Hz for every bars at 120, 125, 128, 144 and 150 BPM, never at 130, 132, 135, 138, 140, 142 or 145; at 44100 Hz for every bars at 120, 125, 126, 135, 140, 144, 147 and 150, at 128 only from 2 bars, never at 130, 132, 138, 142 or 145. Otherwise the file is up to 0.5 frame off the musical length (Live's warp stretch at most 0.5 / N). loop_mode seamless: the file is exactly N frames, one period of a signal with period N; no fade at either end. loop_mode oneshot: the file has round((4 * bars + tail_beats) * 60 * sr / bpm) frames; the musical end is frame N (first frame of the tail). Cross-field rule A: the file length must be at most 72000 ms: 4 * bars * 60000 / bpm <= 72000 in seamless mode, (4 * bars + tail_beats) * 60000 / bpm <= 72000 in oneshot mode (tail_beats counts in oneshot only; 32 bars need bpm >= 106.67). (2) Seamless construction: every stage is either circular (acts on the N-frame period through its N-point real DFT, or is memoryless, or is periodic with an integer number of cycles per N) or a recursive stage run to steady state (point 8). Nothing free-running in Hz, no partial off the bin grid, no random walk, no end fade. (3) Sources, one period of N frames, stereo: seed sub-streams (audio_engine.dsp.substreams(seed, 8), index fixed so a later layer never changes earlier noise): s0 noise left, s1 noise right, s2 smooth_random movement curve, s3 partial drift curves, s4 grain plan, s5-s7 reserved. Noise (noise_bed, resonant, granular source noise): white Gaussian N-frame streams w0 = s0, w1 = s1; L = w0, R = c * w0 + sqrt(1 - c^2) * w1 with c = 1 - stereo_width (as fx-params); each channel shaped in the DFT domain by the tilt 10^(tilt_db_oct * log2(f / 1000) / 20) for f >= 20 Hz and 0 below 20 Hz, then scaled to the RMS of the white stream. Tonal pitch: f0 = 440 * 2^((note - 69 + cents / 100) / 12); voice v has frequency f_v = f0 * 2^(intervals[v] / 12). Bin locking: a frequency f is realised at bin b = round(f * N / sr) (b >= 1), i.e. at b * sr / N Hz, and synthesised as an exact sinusoid on that bin, so it has exactly b cycles per loop. drone: for each voice, partials k = 1 .. partials at bins round(k * f_v * N / sr) (each rounded on its own), amplitude 10^(brightness_db_oct * log2(k) / 20), dropped if their frequency is above 0.45 * sr; a second copy of each partial detune_bins bins higher (detune_bins 0 = no copy), so each pair beats exactly detune_bins times per loop; both channels get the same partial set, the right channel's phases differ by stereo_width * the left phase offset drawn from s3 (0 = identical channels); each partial's level is multiplied by a drift curve 10^(drift_db / 2 * d(n) / 20), d = a smooth_random curve (point 5) drawn from s3 in partial order. resonant: the noise spectrum times a comb magnitude response, the sum over voices and partials k of |H_bp| of a 2nd-order band-pass with Q res_q (0 dB peak) centred at the EXACT k * f_v (not bin-locked: the noise is periodic anyway), weighted as the drone's partials; no detune, no drift (detune_bins and drift_db have no effect). granular: source = granular_source rendered by the rules above (noise = the noise source; drone = the drone source; metal = the hat-params metal_bank partial set scaled so its lowest partial is f0, each a band-limited square with odd harmonics, bin-locked, above 0.45 * sr dropped, the six squares averaged), then K = max(1, round(grain_density * N / sr)) Hann grains of G = round(grain_ms * sr / 1000) frames; for grain i = 0 .. K-1 four values are drawn from s4 in this order: onset o uniform integer in [0, N), read offset u uniform in [-1, 1], pitch p uniform in [-grain_pitch_cents, grain_pitch_cents], pan q uniform in [-grain_pan, grain_pan]; the grain reads the source at (o + u * grain_spread * N / 2 + j * 2^(p / 1200)) mod N (linear interpolation, j = 0 .. G-1), is panned equal-power (gL = cos((q + 1) * pi / 4), gR = sin((q + 1) * pi / 4)) and added at frames (o + j) mod N, grains summed in index order. (4) Fixed filters, circular, zero phase, on the sources: hp |H| = (f / hp_hz)^2 / sqrt(1 + (f / hp_hz)^4), lp |H| = 1 / sqrt(1 + (f / lp_hz)^4) (2nd-order Butterworth magnitudes) applied to the DFT bins. Cross-field rule B: lp_hz >= 1.5 * hp_hz. (5) Movement curve c(n), n = 0 .. N-1, in [-1, 1] with move_cycles cycles per loop: sine c = sin(2 * pi * move_cycles * n / N) (phase 0 at frame 0); smooth_random c = sum over h = 1 .. 4 of a_h * sin(2 * pi * h * move_cycles * n / N + phi_h) with a_h uniform in [0, 1] / h and phi_h uniform in [0, 2 pi) drawn from s2 (a_1, phi_1, a_2, ...), divided by max |sum| (if that max is 0, c = 0); move_cycles 0 = c = 0 (static). One curve drives filter, level and pan. (6) Moving filter: filter_mode off = no stage (filter_hz, filter_q and move_depth_oct have no effect); otherwise ONE time-varying 2nd-order filter whose cutoff is updated every sample, the topology-preserving-transform state-variable filter (Zavalishin) as fx-params point 3: Q = filter_q, bp = band-pass output times 1 / filter_q (0 dB peak gain), lp, hp. Cutoff track fc(n) = filter_hz * 2^(move_depth_oct / 2 * c(n)), so move_depth_oct is the peak-to-peak range in octaves around the centre filter_hz; its lowest value is fc_min = filter_hz * 2^(-move_depth_oct / 2), its highest fc_max = filter_hz * 2^(move_depth_oct / 2). Cross-field rule D (filter_mode not off): fc_min >= 20 and fc_max <= 0.45 * sr. (7) Level and pan: gain in dB = amp_move_db / 2 * c(n) (amp_move_db is peak-to-peak); pan gL = sqrt(1 - pan_move * c(n)), gR = sqrt(1 + pan_move * c(n)) (L and R in opposite phase, constant summed power). Pump: gain 1 - pump_depth * (1 - phi)^4, phi = fractional part of n / spb with spb = 60 * sr / bpm (frame 0 is a beat start); 0 = off. (8) Steady state of the recursive stages (moving filter, reverb), seamless mode: each recursive stage is run on its own: its input period is tiled P + 1 times, the stage runs from zero state over all copies, and the LAST period is kept as the stage output (the next stage gets that exact period). Warm-up count P per stage, from the stage's slowest decay (#525 review point 2; the time constant decides, not a fixed one loop): with T_loop = N / sr seconds, moving filter: tau = filter_q / (pi * fc_min) (time constant 2Q / omega of the slowest pole at the lowest cutoff; Q >= 0.5 so the poles' real part is -omega / (2Q)), P_filter = ceil(20 * tau / T_loop) (e^-20 = -174 dB, margin below the 24-bit LSB, also for the critically damped Q 0.5); worst corner fc_min 20 Hz, Q 12, 1 bar at 200 BPM: tau = 0.191 s, T_loop = 1.2 s, P_filter = 4. Reverb: P_reverb = ceil((2.4 * reverb_decay_ms + reverb_predelay_ms) / 1000 / T_loop) (2.4 * T60 = -144 dB); reverb_mix 0 = no stage, P_reverb 0. Convergence guard: the engine runs one more copy and rejects its own output (error, no file) if the kept period and the next one differ by 1 LSB of bit_depth relative to the final peak or more; the sidecar records preroll_loops per stage. The reverb's energy match (laser_fx.reverb_wet semantics) is computed on the kept period, not on the tiled block. (9) Order: sources (point 3) -> tilt and fixed hp / lp (point 4) -> moving filter (point 6) -> level and pan movement (point 7) -> drive (the kick's anti-aliased saturation, per channel; 0 = off) -> plus reverb_mix * reverb (laser_fx.reverb_wet semantics, steady state per point 8; reverb_damp_hz from 300 Hz) -> pump -> mono_below (side signal S = (L - R) / 2 times w(f) in the DFT domain, w = 0 for f <= mono_below_hz, 1 for f >= mono_below_hz * 2^0.5, linear in log2 f between (half-octave ramp); 0 = off) -> peak scaling. (10) Oneshot mode: the same sources and circular stages on one period; then a linear fade-in from 0 over the first round(fade_in_beats * 60 * sr / bpm) frames and a linear fade-out to 0 ending at frame N (fade_out_beats), then zeros up to the file length (the tail); the recursive stages run once from zero state over the whole file (no warm-up), so tails ring into the tail region; mono_below acts on the file zero-padded by round(sr) frames (cut back afterwards); a 5 ms linear fade-out ends at the last frame (as fx point 6) before the peak scaling. Cross-field rule E (oneshot): fade_in_beats + fade_out_beats <= 4 * bars. In seamless mode fade_in_beats, fade_out_beats and tail_beats have no effect. (11) Tuning rule C (drone, and granular with granular_source drone or metal): the realised fundamental b0 * sr / N with b0 = round(f0 * N / sr) misses f0 by |1200 * log2(b0 * sr / (N * f0))| cents; rejected if that exceeds max_tuning_cents. The bin spacing is sr / N ~ bpm / (240 * bars) Hz, and the miss can reach half a bin, so short loops at low notes can fail (1 bar at 200 BPM and 48 kHz: N = 57600, bin 0.833 Hz; half a bin at note 24, 32.70 Hz, is 21.9 cents up / 22.2 cents down, above the 20 maximum; note 24 itself lands on bin 39, 10.8 cents flat). At the default 8 bars every note passes the default 5 cents (half a bin at most 2.8 cents at note 24, 200 BPM). resonant is not bin-locked and is not checked. (12) Peak: the whole file is scaled so the peak of the QUANTISED file is peak_ceiling_dbfs within one LSB and never above (as fx-params point 9); level against a kick is set in Live (note A6). (13) Determinism: same resolved parameters (including seed) give a byte-identical WAV on every CI platform; variants as laser-params. (14) Reject out-of-range values, never clamp. Reject cross-field rules A, B, C, D and E with an error text. Defaults are placeholders until measured. (15) Sidecar: category 'atmos', engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-atmos' with its own version (D-025); the sample-metadata entry is category 'atmos' (#529 step 0) with the required features loop_samples (N), loop_samples_exact (240 * bars * sr / bpm), seamless and preroll_loops ({filter, reverb}, point 8) and the optional tuning_error_cents and realised_detune_cents. Shared field names keep the meaning of fx-params v0.1 / laser-params v0.2 (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, peak_ceiling_dbfs, stereo_width, drive, pump_depth, filter_mode, filter_q, reverb_*, preset); documented differences: filter_mode has 'off' and no 'hp_lp'; filter_hz is the centre of a movement, not a start/end pair; reverb_decay_ms up to 12000 (fx 8000); reverb_damp_hz from 300 (laser / fx 1000) so the 400 Hz 'dark' variant (note A2) is reachable; stereo_width default 0.7 (fx 0.6).

seed.description: Seeds the noise, movement, drift and grain sub-streams ($comment point 3). Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV.

bpm.description: Required: the loop length is in bars at this tempo ($comment point 1).

kind.description: Which sources are rendered ($comment point 3) and the per-kind defaults (allOf).

bars.description: Loop length in 4/4 bars: N = round(240 * bars * sample_rate / bpm) frames (cross-field rule A: at most 72000 ms).

loop_mode.description: seamless = the file is one period and loops without a seam; oneshot = fades and an optional tail ($comment point 10).

fade_in_beats.description: oneshot only: linear fade-in from the first frame, beats. fade_in_beats + fade_out_beats <= 4 * bars (cross-field rule E).

fade_out_beats.description: oneshot only: linear fade-out ending at the musical end (frame N), beats.

tail_beats.description: oneshot only: filter and reverb tail after the musical end, beats; counts in rule A.

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Peak of the quantised file after scaling ($comment point 12).

hp_hz.description: Fixed circular high-pass, 2nd-order magnitude, zero phase (per-kind default). lp_hz >= 1.5 * hp_hz (cross-field rule B).

lp_hz.description: Fixed circular low-pass, 2nd-order magnitude, zero phase (per-kind default).

tilt_db_oct.description: Spectral tilt of the noise source, dB per octave around 1 kHz; -3 = pink.

stereo_width.description: 0 = mono sources; 1 = independent L/R noise (correlation 1 - stereo_width), as fx-params.

mono_below_hz.description: Side signal removed below this frequency (half-octave ramp, $comment point 9). 0 = off.

filter_mode.description: Moving filter (per-kind default): one time-varying state-variable filter ($comment point 6). off = no moving filter.

filter_hz.description: Centre cutoff of the moving filter (bp: centre frequency), Hz (per-kind default). The cutoff moves move_depth_oct / 2 octaves above and below it (cross-field rule D).

filter_q.description: Q of the moving filter (per-kind default). Sets its warm-up length together with the lowest cutoff ($comment point 8).

move_cycles.description: Whole cycles of the movement curve per loop (per-kind default). 0 = static. At 8 bars, 2 = one cycle per 4 bars.

move_shape.description: sine, or a seeded periodic sum of the first 4 harmonics of move_cycles ($comment point 5).

move_depth_oct.description: Peak-to-peak range of the moving filter's cutoff, octaves, centred on filter_hz (per-kind default).

amp_move_db.description: Peak-to-peak level movement, dB, same curve (per-kind default).

pan_move.description: Auto-pan depth, same curve, L/R in opposite phase. 0 = off.

pump_depth.description: Level dip on every beat, frame 0 is a beat start. 0 = off.

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation, same stage as kick drive, per channel. 0 = off.

note.description: Tonal kinds: MIDI note of the root (36 = C2, 65.41 Hz).

intervals.description: Voices in semitones above the root; the first is 0 (root, fifth, octave by default).

partials.description: Harmonics per voice, each bin-locked; above 0.45 * sample_rate dropped.

brightness_db_oct.description: Partial level slope per octave of harmonic number.

detune_bins.description: drone: a second copy of each partial this many DFT bins higher, beating exactly detune_bins times per loop. 0 = off.

drift_db.description: drone: peak-to-peak slow level drift per partial (seeded, periodic).

max_tuning_cents.description: Tuning rule C: the request is rejected if the bin-locked fundamental misses the note by more than this ($comment point 11).

res_q.description: resonant: Q of the band-pass at each partial (circular magnitude response on the noise).

granular_source.description: granular: the internal source the grains read ($comment point 3).

grain_pitch_cents.description: granular: seeded per-grain pitch offset, up to this many cents either way.

grain_spread.description: granular: source read position scatter around the grain's own onset, share of the loop (0 = read in place).

reverb_mix.description: Relative send level of the reverb (1 = wet energy equals dry energy), as laser v0.2 (per-kind default). 0 = off.

reverb_decay_ms.description: Reverb decay (T60) as laser v0.2, extended to 12000 ms (fx 8000). Sets the reverb warm-up ($comment point 8).

reverb_damp_hz.description: High-frequency damping corner inside the reverb, Hz. Floor 300 (laser / fx 1000) so the 400 Hz 'dark' variant of note A2 is in range.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.

allOf.$comment: noise_bed defaults; also applies when kind is omitted (noise_bed is the default kind)
